rulings.docket_item: p02-013 (cluster c05, span Eccl.7.2-Eccl.7.4): after the mandated re-tiering, does a correctly-tiered cohesion warrant clear the cluster bar, or does the row revert to atomic single_saying rows?
rulings.decision: NO BOUNDARY CHANGE -- the saying_cluster STANDS at web:Eccl.7.2-Eccl.7.4 (exact span set: { "Eccl.7.2-Eccl.7.4" }). The peer's tier finding is upheld in full and the row's stated warrant is STRUCK, but a correctly-tiered warrant that clears the B-4 bar is already carried by the row's own bytes and is substituted for it; disclosure cures are mandatory and the medium_low hold is capped, not raised.
rulings.grounds: Re-derived independently with the staged collator. TIER: the bracket phrase spliced from oshb:Eccl.7.2, "בֵּֽית אֵ֗בֶל", collates BYTE against oshb:Eccl.7.2 but only SKELETON against oshb:Eccl.7.4, whose own attested form carries the prefixed preposition, "בְּבֵ֣ית אֵ֔בֶל" (oshb:Eccl.7.4, byte tier from its own verse) -- so the row's 'recurs verbatim' and its device_notes claim of 'byte-verified at both' are false at the tier they assert; the peer's finding is confirmed. But the driver, correctly tiered, is STRONGER than the row claimed on the measure that actually decides a boundary. The mourning lexeme is word-bound identical across the two ends at SKELETON tier and collates ACCENT_STRIPPED as a pointed form ( "אֵ֗בֶל" oshb:Eccl.7.2 against "אֵ֔בֶל" oshb:Eccl.7.4 ), and its distribution is maximally discriminating: sweep of the word-bound consonantal form returns exactly 2 verses book-wide -- web:Eccl.7.2 and web:Eccl.7.4 -- with ZERO occurrences anywhere else in the book, i.e. 2 of 2 inside the row's own span; the contiguous two-word phrase likewise returns exactly those 2 verses. The phrase collates NONE against both excluded neighbours, oshb:Eccl.7.1 and oshb:Eccl.7.5. That clears conditions 1-4 of the B-4 standard. Internal chaining is real though thin: the word-bound content-token intersection is non-empty at EVERY adjacent pair inside the span -- verses 2/3 share the tov token, verses 3/4 share the heart token, 1 token each (skeleton tier), which is the low-confidence register's own named thin-cohesion case, not a disqualification. RIVAL, disclosed and argued past: the laughter root is a contiguous substring at exactly 2 verses book-wide, web:Eccl.7.3 and web:Eccl.7.6 ("שְׂחֹ֣ק", oshb:Eccl.7.6, byte tier from its own verse) -- an interlocking rival envelope over verses 3-6 that straddles this row's closing seam and is as exclusive as the mourning envelope; it fails as a unit driver because a 3-6 span's own adjacent chain BREAKS at 5/6, whose word-bound intersection is empty (re-derived; the same emptiness that decides B-2). UNDISCLOSED CLOSING-SEAM ECHOES, confirmed: the fools token is word-bound identical across oshb:Eccl.7.4 and oshb:Eccl.7.5 ("כְּסִילִ֖ים" / "כְּסִילִֽים", collating skeleton across the pair -- accent-stripped separation only because the second carries silluq, which the accent-stripped tier retains; sweep: 3 verses book-wide carry that word-bound form, web:Eccl.7.4, web:Eccl.7.5, web:Eccl.7.9), and a wise-ROOT family bridges web:Eccl.7.4, web:Eccl.7.5 and web:Eccl.7.7 across TWO attested spellings, which no single substring sweep catches because of final-letter allography -- the word-bound plural at web:Eccl.7.4 (sweep: 3 verses book-wide) and the word-bound singular at web:Eccl.7.5 and web:Eccl.7.7 (sweep: 7 verses book-wide, exactly 2 of them in this chapter) -- all standing against the row's flat 'a different topic' framing for its closing seam.

consequence.spec: NO boundary change; keep span web:Eccl.7.2-Eccl.7.4, unit_type saying_cluster, parent_collection "M Eccl.1.12-Eccl.12.7", confidence CAPPED at medium_low (unchanged). Install as ONE pass on p02-013: (1) STRIKE the tier overclaims -- 'recurs verbatim' in boundary_rationale and 'byte tier, byte-verified at both' in device_notes; replace with the true per-end tiers: byte at the first verse, skeleton at the second, and disclose the exact form difference (bare construct at web:Eccl.7.2, prefixed preposition at web:Eccl.7.4). (2) SWAP the named warrant to the one the bytes carry: the mourning lexeme is word-bound identical at skeleton tier across the two ends (accent-stripped as a pointed form) and is book-exclusive to this span -- cite the exclusivity digit (sweep: 2 verses book-wide, both inside the span, zero elsewhere), which is what discriminates BOTH seams; the phrase matches neither neighbour at any tier. (3) ADD the internal-chain disclosure: every adjacent pair inside the span shares exactly one word-bound content token (tov across verses 2/3; heart across verses 3/4) -- the honest thin-cohesion hold, stated as such, which is what the medium_low is for. (4) DISCLOSE and argue past the closing-seam echoes rather than asserting 'a different topic': the fools token word-bound identical into web:Eccl.7.5 (sweep: 3 verses book-wide), the wise-family lexeme into web:Eccl.7.5 and web:Eccl.7.7, and the laughter root's rival envelope at exactly 2 verses book-wide (web:Eccl.7.3, web:Eccl.7.6) straddling this seam -- rebut it on the byte ground ruled here, that the rival span's own chain breaks at the token-empty 5/6 seam while this span's chain holds at every adjacent pair. (5) strongest_rejected_alternative stays one sentence plus at most the one mandated rival sentence; the rival it must now carry is the laughter-envelope respan, not only the whole-chapter tov-anaphora cluster it currently argues. (6) boundary_evidence_refs must mirror every verse argued outside the span (web:Eccl.7.1, web:Eccl.7.5, web:Eccl.7.6, web:Eccl.7.7, web:Eccl.7.9 -- verse 9 is newly argued and must be added). TEST the cure must pass (the test that killed the original): the cited bracket phrase must re-collate to byte tier against BOTH cited refs before any 'verbatim' or 'byte-verified at both' label may stand -- it does not, so the label must be the true tier; and every seam-adjacent device the row's own bytes carry must be disclosed at least as completely as any device the row cites in its favour.

rulings.docket_item: p02-014 (cluster c05, span Eccl.7.5-Eccl.7.6): does a genuinely discriminating byte-grounded cohesion driver exist, or does the row revert to atomic rows under the sentence zone's hybrid-atomic default?
rulings.decision: BOUNDARY CHANGE ADOPTED -- the row reverts to atomic single_saying rows. Exact new span set: { "Eccl.7.5-Eccl.7.5", "Eccl.7.6-Eccl.7.6" }. No discriminating driver exists: the members' word-bound content-token intersection is empty, and the only lexeme in the neighbourhood binds the excluded neighbour more tightly than it binds the pair.
rulings.grounds: The B-4 floor is not reached and condition 3 fails decisively. FLOOR: the word-bound content-token intersection of the two members is EMPTY, re-derived from the consonantal skeletons -- oshb:Eccl.7.5 and oshb:Eccl.7.6 share 0 tokens, function words included; there is no catchword, no repeated phrase, and no construction run to name, so no byte-grounded cohesion driver exists to satisfy the sentence zone's cluster bar. DISCRIMINATION: the only lexical recurrence available anywhere near this pair (every adjacent word-bound intersection across web:Eccl.7.1-Eccl.7.8 re-derived) is the fool lexeme, and it binds the EXCLUDED NEIGHBOUR strictly more tightly than it binds the row's own members. Re-derived: "כְּסִילִֽים" (oshb:Eccl.7.5) collates SKELETON against oshb:Eccl.7.4 -- word-bound identity, the same attested plural ("כְּסִילִ֖ים", oshb:Eccl.7.4) -- but collates NONE against oshb:Eccl.7.6, whose form is the definite singular ("הַכְּסִ֑יל", oshb:Eccl.7.6, byte tier from its own verse); across the row's own seam the match survives only as a contained consonantal substring across an article-plus-number difference (sweep: the lexeme as substring at 4 ch-7 verses -- web:Eccl.7.4, 7.5, 7.6, 7.9; the word-bound plural at 3 verses book-wide -- web:Eccl.7.4, 7.5, 7.9). A driver that ties the row's opening verse backward to the verse the row excludes, at a stronger tier than it ties the row's own pair together, is texture, not a boundary driver. The row's ACTUALLY NAMED driver -- the verse-initial causal particle at the second member -- fails the same condition, confirming the peer: "כִּ֣י" (oshb:Eccl.7.6) collates ACCENT_STRIPPED against oshb:Eccl.7.7, whose own opening token is the identical particle ("כִּ֥י", oshb:Eccl.7.7, byte tier from its own verse) -- the particle heads both the verse it is asked to bind inward and the very neighbour the row is held apart from (sweep: 5 verse-initial sites in this chapter). The operative-category law's one-sentence rescue is unavailable: the first member is a complete comparative saying and the second is a separate sentence that closes on the book's own vanity tag, so this is not a syntactically-continuous single sentence spanning two verses. The row's rejected_alternative is additionally byte-false in claiming the excluded neighbour shares no vocabulary -- the word-bound singular wise-token is identical across oshb:Eccl.7.5 and oshb:Eccl.7.7 (sweep: 7 verses book-wide, and these are the only 2 in this chapter). With no driver clearing the bar, the sentence zone's single_saying default controls.

consequence.spec: ADOPTED BOUNDARY CHANGE. p02-014 is RETIRED. EXACT NEW SPAN SET, tiling web:Eccl.7.5-Eccl.7.6 with no gap or overlap: { "Eccl.7.5-Eccl.7.5", "Eccl.7.6-Eccl.7.6" } -- two atomic rows, unit_type single_saying, parent_collection "M Eccl.1.12-Eccl.12.7" on both, full X-X span form on both, new decision_ids assigned by the author wave in canonical order (chunk_index renumbered at assembly). REQUIRED CONTENT. Row Eccl.7.5-Eccl.7.5: ground the atomic verdict on the token-empty forward seam (word-bound intersection with the following verse is empty, re-derived), NOT on any claim of isolation -- and disclose, on the same row, the backward fools-token identity into web:Eccl.7.4 (sweep: 3 verses book-wide carry that word-bound form) and the wise-lexeme identity forward into web:Eccl.7.7, arguing past both on the topic ground rather than denying them. Row Eccl.7.6-Eccl.7.6: ground the atomic verdict on the vanity-tag close, which terminates the saying, and disclose that its opening causal particle does not discriminate its seams because the following verse opens with the identical particle (sweep: 5 verse-initial sites in this chapter); it may cite the causal dependence on the preceding verse as texture in device_notes, never as a boundary driver. NEITHER row may assert that a neighbour shares no vocabulary. SEAM-PAIR SYMMETRY: this is ONE edit installed on both rows -- the 7:5|7:6 seam disclosure must read identically in substance from both sides. COLLATERAL: p02-013 needs no respan from this change, but its closing-seam disclosure ordered under B-1 must name the same fools-token identity, so install B-1 and B-2 in one pass. VERIFY: exact tiling of web:Eccl.7.5-Eccl.7.6 re-checked; parent seams untouched. TEST each replacement warrant must pass (the test that killed the original): the word-bound content-token intersection of any span claimed as a cluster must be non-empty and named, and any verse-initial-particle or lexeme warrant must be collated against the immediately excluded neighbour's own bytes and must not bind that neighbour at an equal or stronger tier.

rulings.docket_item: P03-023 + P03-024 (cluster c10, spans Eccl.11.1-Eccl.11.2 and Eccl.11.3-Eccl.11.6): ONE decision for the 11:1-6 zone -- do the two admonition_unit rows stand with cures, or is a merger/respan adopted?
rulings.decision: MERGER ADOPTED -- one admonition_unit row for the whole zone. Exact new span set: { "Eccl.11.1-Eccl.11.6" }, replacing both rows. The imperative/jussive-frame derivation the law requires yields a single frame whose directives stand at 11:1, 11:2 and 11:6 around a directive-free middle; three separate byte-grounded binders cross the seam the split draws; and neither existing row is internally as well bound as the seam that divides them.
rulings.grounds: The B-4 cluster standard does NOT govern here and is not applied: these are admonition_unit rows in monologue territory, not saying_cluster rows in a sentence zone. The controlling law is the admonition clause, which names the 11:1-6 zone as the imperative-counsel candidate and requires the bounds to be ARGUED FROM THE IMPERATIVE/JUSSIVE FRAMES. Re-derived from the pointed bytes, that frame decides the question against the split. DIRECTIVE DISTRIBUTION: the zone's directive forms stand at its two ENDS -- "שַׁלַּ֥ח" (oshb:Eccl.11.1, byte tier), "תֶּן" (oshb:Eccl.11.2, byte tier), and at the close "זְרַ֣ע" with the negative "אַל תַּנַּ֣ח" (oshb:Eccl.11.6, byte tier) -- while the middle three verses carry no second-person directive at all (a conditional protasis at verse 3, a participial clause with a negated prefix-conjugation at verse 4, a comparative declarative at verse 5). A split at 11:2|11:3 therefore severs the imperative frame from its own closing member and leaves the second row imperative-HEADLESS across its first three verses -- the derivation the law asks for produces one frame, not two. REFRAIN ACROSS THE SEVERED SEAM, with the tiers corrected (the peer labelled both of these byte; they are not): "לֹ֣א תֵדַ֔ע" (oshb:Eccl.11.2) collates ACCENT_STRIPPED against oshb:Eccl.11.5 ("לֹ֤א תֵדַע֙"), and "אֵֽינְךָ֤ יוֹדֵ֨עַ֙" (oshb:Eccl.11.5) collates SKELETON against oshb:Eccl.11.6 ("אֵֽינְךָ֨ יוֹדֵ֜ע"). Controlling count objects and digit pairs, re-swept as contiguous consonantal substrings: the know-negation of the first form = 2 verses book-wide (web:Eccl.11.2, web:Eccl.11.5); the negated-existential form = 2 verses book-wide (web:Eccl.11.5, web:Eccl.11.6). Both objects are book-EXCLUSIVE to this zone, and they interlock 11:2 -> 11:5 -> 11:6, crossing the proposed seam. The second row already CONCEDES this carry-through in its own rationale and never rebuts it -- a disclosed but unanswered continuity admission. REPEATED PHRASE ON THE SEAM ITSELF: "עַל הָאָֽרֶץ" (oshb:Eccl.11.2) and "עַל הָאָ֣רֶץ" (oshb:Eccl.11.3) -- a word-bound two-token repetition collating SKELETON across the seam (accent-stripped separation only because the first carries silluq, which that tier retains); sweep: 7 verses book-wide, and 11:2/11:3 is the only ADJACENT pair among them. THIRD BINDER tying the declarative middle to the closing imperative: the sowing root at "יִזְרָ֑ע" (oshb:Eccl.11.4, byte tier) and "זְרַ֣ע" (oshb:Eccl.11.6, byte tier) -- sweep: 2 verses book-wide, both inside the merged span. INTERNAL SEAM COMPARISON, decisive: the two existing rows are each less well bound internally than the seam that divides them -- the first row's own members share 0 content tokens (word-bound intersection = 2 tokens, the causal particle and the preposition, both function words), and the second row's own 11:3|11:4 seam has an EMPTY word-bound intersection, linked only by the cloud lexeme at substring tier (sweep: 3 verses book-wide -- web:Eccl.11.3, web:Eccl.11.4, web:Eccl.12.2) (sweep: 3 verses book-wide -- web:Eccl.11.3, web:Eccl.11.4, web:Eccl.12.2). There is no byte warrant for the split that the merged span does not also carry. OUTER BOUNDS CLEAN: the back seam 10:20|11:1 shares only the causal particle (function word) and 10:20 closes the second sentence zone; the forward seam 11:6|11:7 shares only the object marker, and 11:7 opens the light-frame of the aging-allegory zone (count object: sun-lexeme verses standing OUTSIDE the under-the-sun formula -- sweep: 5 verses book-wide, web:Eccl.11.7 among them; the formula is a separate object at 27 verses and reaches no ch-11 verse).

consequence.spec: ADOPTED BOUNDARY CHANGE -- ONE decision for the whole 11:1-6 zone. P03-023 and P03-024 are RETIRED and replaced by a SINGLE row. EXACT NEW SPAN SET: { "Eccl.11.1-Eccl.11.6" }. unit_type admonition_unit; parent_collection "M Eccl.1.12-Eccl.12.7" (no parent seam straddled); confidence CAPPED at medium_low (the merged span contains the bread-on-waters crux, a named expected-low-confidence region); new decision_id assigned in canonical order, chunk_index renumbered at assembly. REQUIRED CONTENT of the merged row. (1) boundary_rationale must perform the imperative/jussive-frame derivation the law requires, not assert it: name the directive forms at the zone's two ends with pointed splices and byte-tier labels, state that the middle three verses carry no second-person directive, and argue the frame as the unit's bounds. (2) Name the negated-knowledge refrain as the internal binder with its TRUE tiers -- accent-stripped between the first and middle occurrence, skeleton between the middle and last -- and carry both exclusivity digits (each attested form: sweep 2 verses book-wide, all four sites inside this span). NO byte label may be attached to either cross-verse recurrence. (3) Name the repeated on-the-earth phrase across 11:2/11:3 (skeleton tier; sweep 7 verses book-wide, the only adjacent pair among them) and the sowing root across 11:4/11:6 (sweep 2 verses book-wide, both inside the span) as the binders that carry the previously severed seam. (4) Argue both outer bounds from content: the token-clean back seam at 10:20|11:1 and the forward seam at 11:6|11:7 where the light-frame of the aging-allegory zone begins -- never from chapter numbering, which is forbidden-tier. (5) observed_substrate_signals: STRIKE the chasing-wind and wind-thought citations outright -- neither device object contains ANY ch-11 verse (7 verses and 2 verses respectively, re-confirmed), and this span carries only literal wind/breath forms; if a wind signal is wanted, cite the any-ruach object accurately (sweep: 20 verses book-wide) and name the literal, non-idiomatic sense at web:Eccl.11.4 and web:Eccl.11.5. (6) strongest_rejected_alternative: one sentence rejecting the now-inverted rival -- that web:Eccl.11.1-Eccl.11.2 stands as its own admonition_unit -- rebutted FROM BYTES (its two members share no content token, while the refrain and the on-the-earth phrase both carry across 11:2|11:3), plus at most the one mandated-rival sentence; no third sentence. (7) device_notes: hold the bread-on-waters referent crux honestly and bespoke; the wind/cloud imagery stays texture. (8) boundary_evidence_refs must mirror every verse argued outside the span (web:Eccl.10.20, web:Eccl.11.7). VERIFY: exact tiling of web:Eccl.11.1-Eccl.11.6 with the neighbouring rows re-checked; no parent seam straddled. SWEEP, not a spot fix -- the mis-cited-device-object class is systemic: re-check observed_substrate_signals on ALL 85 draft rows and strike or correct every inventory object that contains no verse inside its own row's span. TEST the cure must pass (the test that killed the originals): no device the row's own bytes carry across a seam the row draws may be left disclosed but un-rebutted; every cited device-inventory object must contain at least one verse of the row's own span; and the admonition bounds must be shown to follow from the directive forms rather than asserted.

rulings.docket_item: CROSS-CLUSTER STANDARD (c05+c09): does a cohesion driver matching only at SKELETON tier satisfy the 'byte-grounded cohesion evidence NAMED' bar for saying_cluster rows once the tier is honestly disclosed, or does the bar require byte-tier identity / multiple independent drivers? Apply consistently in B-1/B-2 and state its bearing on P03-015 (c09).
rulings.decision: STANDARD SETTLED DECISION-LOCALLY (no owner escalation; the governing text does not underdetermine it -- its own named exemplar decides it). A cohesion driver that matches only at SKELETON tier DOES satisfy the 'byte-grounded cohesion evidence NAMED' bar for saying_cluster rows in the two sentence zones. 'Byte-grounded' means derived from the source bytes and quotable to a NAMED tier -- it does not mean byte-tier identity, and it does not require multiple independent drivers. The bar is met when ONE named driver clears four conditions: (1) TIER HONESTY -- the matched tier is named per cited ref, and every form difference (prefix, article, number, gender, accent) is disclosed; 'verbatim' / 'byte-verified at both' is available only where the splice collates byte at EVERY ref it is cited against. (2) WORD-BOUNDING -- the driver is a word-bound token or phrase recurrence, or, where it is a contained substring across a morpheme boundary, it is stated as such and the shared lexeme is named. (3) DISCRIMINATION -- the driver must separate the row's own seams: it may not bind an immediately excluded neighbor at a tier equal to or stronger than the tier at which it binds the row's own members; and the citation must carry an EXCLUSIVITY digit (verses book-wide carrying the driver, and how many of those lie inside the span), which is the measure that actually discriminates a boundary. (4) NON-THEMATIC -- a lexical or constructional recurrence, never a shared theme. SUFFICIENCY: one driver clearing (1)-(4) admits the cluster. Where the members' word-bound content-token intersection is EMPTY and no construction run replaces it, no driver has been named at all and the row falls to the single_saying default. Where a driver clears the bar but adjacent-pair cohesion is thinner than two shared content tokens, the row is ADMITTED and CAPPED at medium_low with a bespoke honest hold -- the low-confidence register is a confidence-and-disclosure consequence, never a boundary consequence. Applied unchanged in B-1 (admits), B-2 (fails at condition 3 and on the empty-intersection floor), and B-3-adjacent P03-015 (admits; peer's no-boundary-change ruling CONFIRMED).
rulings.grounds: Dispositive from the governing text's own named exemplar. The strategy names the 7:1-8 tov-opener anaphora as the expected legitimate cluster case. Re-derived: the opening token spliced from oshb:Eccl.7.2, "ט֞וֹב", collates at ACCENT_STRIPPED tier -- never byte -- against oshb:Eccl.7.1 ("ט֥וֹב"), oshb:Eccl.7.5 and oshb:Eccl.7.11, and at oshb:Eccl.7.11 the attested form is feminine ("טוֹבָ֥ה"), so the exemplar is not even a skeleton-token identity at all of its members; the count object is 'verses whose first skeleton token is the tov/tova form' (sweep: 12 verses book-wide, 7 of them in ch 7). Masoretic accentuation is position-dependent, so a cross-verse recurrence of a single accented word collates byte only where the accents happen to coincide. A byte-identity bar would therefore void the law's own exemplar at every one of its 7 in-chapter members -- a reading that is unavailable, and the reason the question is settled here rather than escalated. Nor is a multiple-driver bar available: the text says 'cohesion evidence NAMED' (singular), and the low-confidence register expressly anticipates admitted cluster rows whose cohesion is thinner than two shared content tokens, i.e. admitted-and-held, not refused. What the bar DOES carry is the anti-over-clustering clause ('a cluster whose only glue is a shared THEME is over-clustering'), which is condition 4, and the standing cross-seam rule, which is condition 3: a byte-true device straddling a row's own seam argues continuity against the row unless disclosed and argued past. Tier arithmetic confirming the standard bites in both directions, re-derived here: the P03-015 advantage lexeme spliced from oshb:Eccl.10.11, "יִתְר֔וֹן", collates ACCENT_STRIPPED into oshb:Eccl.10.10, while oshb:Eccl.10.10's own conjunctive-vav-prefixed form, "וְיִתְר֥וֹן", collates NONE against oshb:Eccl.10.11 -- direction-dependent, hence a contained-substring lexeme recurrence across a morpheme boundary under condition 2, not a word-bound token identity.

consequence.spec: STANDING STANDARD for the author wave, stated above; it binds every saying_cluster row (8 in the current draft set; 7 after B-2 retires one). CONCRETE CURES ORDERED HERE. (A) P03-015 (web:Eccl.10.10-Eccl.10.11): the peer's no-boundary-change ruling is CONFIRMED under this standard -- span, unit_type saying_cluster and the medium_low hold all stand. Install these edits as ONE pass: (i) re-tier the advantage recurrence -- it is NOT a word-bound token identity across the pair; state that the first member carries the conjunctive-vav-prefixed form and the second the bare form, that the lexeme collates at accent-stripped tier from the second verse into the first and not in the reverse direction, and drop any byte label attached to the CROSS-VERSE recurrence (each verse's own splice keeps its own byte label); (ii) name the second, independent, genuinely discriminating driver the row never cited -- both members open on the same verse-initial conditional particle, spliced as "אִם" (oshb:Eccl.10.10, byte tier) and "אִם" (oshb:Eccl.10.11, byte tier), collating BYTE across the pair (sweep: 6 verse-initial sites book-wide, 3 of them in this chapter -- verses 4, 10 and 11 -- and verses 10/11 the only consecutive pair among all 6); neither web:Eccl.10.9 nor web:Eccl.10.12 carries it; (iii) carry the exclusivity digit for the advantage lexeme (sweep: 9 verses book-wide, one token each, web:Eccl.10.10-Eccl.10.11 the only consecutive pair); (iv) keep the peer's own three cures -- drop the 'closes with' / 'brackets both endings' placement claim (both verses end two tokens past the lexeme), flag or drop the 'too late' gloss as English-rendering-level rather than a claim on the Hebrew privative construction, and add the undisclosed serpent/bite-root cross-seam tie back to web:Eccl.10.8. (B) SWEEP, not a spot fix -- the tier-overclaim class is systemic: re-collate EVERY cross-verse recurrence claim in the whole draft set against EVERY ref it is cited at, and relabel each to its true tier. Four rows currently carry verbatim/byte-verified/byte-identical language on cross-verse recurrences (p02-013, p02-029, p02-030, P03-016); p02-013 is cured under B-1, the other three must be checked and cured in the same pass. TEST each cure must pass (the test that killed the original): a splice may be labelled byte tier at a ref only if collation against that ref's own source bytes returns byte; and every cluster driver must carry its exclusivity digit and be checked against the immediately excluded neighbours' bytes before it is called a boundary marker. Row prose stays register-clean: no section citations, no tool names, no decision-ids; the '(sweep: N verses)' shorthand with the count object named is the sanctioned form.
